rules.title: Source of lawful income discrimination prohibited under NJ Law Against Discrimination
rules.requirement: Landlords may not discriminate in housing based on the source of lawful income or source of lawful rent payment a tenant uses. For example, a landlord cannot refuse to rent to a Section 8 voucher holder solely because of that income source.
rules.key_value: Source of lawful income (e.g., Section 8 vouchers) is a protected basis
rules.quoted_span:
This means, for example, that a landlord cannot deny the
lawful recipient of a Section 8 HUD voucher the right to
rent an apartment based solely on that source of lawful
income.
rules.coverage_text: Applies to the sale or rental of all property, including open land, whether for business or residential purposes, subject to listed exceptions.
rules.exemptions: Rental of a single apartment or flat in a two-family dwelling where the owner occupies the other unit; rental of rooms by the owner or occupant of a one-family dwelling they occupy as a residence; religious organization preference for persons of the same religion; familial status protection does not apply to housing for older persons.
rules.conflict_note: The document describes complaint procedures but states no specific sanction. Complaints may be filed with the Division on Civil Rights within 180 days or in Superior Court within two years.
